conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit words held in the byte-lane RAMs and returned on reads; data-memory operation depends on retaining and supplying these words.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The memory can hold integrator-sensitive or private data, and its contents reach bus_rsp_o.data through rdata at lines 75-78 and 129. The RAM contents are writable from bus_req_i.data at lines 63-72, so an access can modify stored words. Returning stored words is required for data-memory operation, and rden can withhold the read response at line 129.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue unauthorized writes to corrupt stored words, read requests to extract them, or suppress required read data.

conceptual assets.information: The word address derived from the bus request selects which data-memory word is read or written; correct data-memory access depends on this selection.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The access address is security-relevant selection information, and bus_req_i.addr is converted to addr at line 113 and selects RAM locations for reads and writes at lines 63-78, so changing it can redirect an access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter bus_req_i.addr to redirect a write or read to a different memory word.

conceptual assets.information: The registered read-enable decision controls whether a memory read result is presented on bus_rsp_o.data. It has no entry or exit port because request fields only decide it and it only gates the response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The read-release decision is security-sensitive because changing it changes whether requested memory data is delivered, and it is assigned from request fields at line 124. rden directly gates bus_rsp_o.data at line 129, so clearing or blocking it can withhold required read data.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force or suppress the registered read-enable decision so a read response is withheld or delivered on an unintended request.

considered, not kept.reason: The request strobe, read/write direction and byte enables only specify whether the access occurs, its direction and which bytes it changes; access-command fields are not pieces of their own.
The acknowledge only repeats the request strobe at line 125, so it is a bus-handshake copy rather than information of its own.
The error field is tied to constant zero at line 130 and therefore carries no runtime information or asset-relevant behavior.
The AMO, debug, fence, lock, privilege and source fields occur only in the port declaration at line 28 and are not read or used by this unit.
clk_i only times assignments at lines 60, 88 and 123, and the clock-exclusion rule bars it as a conceptual asset.
rstn_i only resets rden and the response acknowledge at lines 120-122, and reset inputs are excluded as conceptual assets.
DMEM_SIZE and alt_style_c are build-time values at lines 22-24 and 36, so no element can change or withhold them at run time.
